text: RAF Fairford incident involves 'foreign actor', says Rubio, as some evacuated residents return home
The secretary of state, who did not provide further details, was speaking to US media after five men arrested on suspicion of terror offences were released on bail.
OpenAI scraps rollout of new model over safety concerns
The firm also issued an update on incidents in which its models accessed Australian government systems.
Sir Ranulph Fiennes' relatives tell BBC it's 'very painful' not being able to visit him
It has been alleged that Sir Ranulph has been admitted to a number of care homes under assumed names.
'We don't know where he is,' relatives of Sir Ranulph Fiennes tell BBC
Speaking to BBC Newsnight, his former sister-in-law told the BBC that she did not know where he was, and nobody had been able to see him.
Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott jailed for child sexual abuse
He was sentenced to seven years in prison after being found guilty of two charges of lewd and libidinous behaviour towards a girl and a boy between 1993 and 2010.
Are Trump's US government funded ads illegal?
President Trump has faced criticism after fronting adverts which were paid for by the US government.
Evicted Spanish pensioner can move back home, lawyer says
The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal, 87, prompted large-scale protests across Spain.
Only from the BBC
A virtual power plant hidden in Vermont homes is keeping the lights on during storms
Spread across thousands of ordinary homes, this "power plant" has become Vermont's largest power source. It's protecting owners from outages and providing cheaper, cleaner energy.
The heroic US lawyer who put Nazi death squad members on trial at Nuremberg
On 29 September 1947, the "biggest murder trial in history" began. Seventy years on, the chief prosecutor, Ben Ferencz, told the BBC how he fought to bring 22 killers to justice.
